caption: Is this talk for me? What should I learn first?
voiceover: A conference schedule tells you when and where. It doesn't tell you whether you're ready. Advanced talks assume things you might not know, and the session that teaches them might be earlier, at the same time, or nowhere. Throughline answers one question: what should I learn before this talk, and where?
actions: Landing page, cursor rests near the city box.

caption: Find your conference: a Bright Data web search, cached for 48 hours
voiceover: Start by finding your conference. Nearby conferences come from a Bright Data web search, cached for two days, so this one is instant. OpenAI picks out real conferences, only from links the search returned, and the dates are checked in code. Conferences we haven't loaded say so honestly. GitHub Universe, next week, is ready now.
actions: Type 'San Francisco, CA', click Search, show Near results and Ready now.

caption: The whole conference as a graph: arrows mean 'prepares you for'
voiceover: This is the whole conference as a graph. Talks run left to right in time. An arrow means this talk prepares you for that one: it teaches something the later talk assumes, and it ends before the later one starts. Hover a talk, and its chain lights up.
actions: Open the map for GitHub Universe, hover a talk with a long chain.

caption: Tell it your goal, in your own words
voiceover: Now, tell it your goal in your own words: I'm new to MCP, and I want to build my first server. The agent maps that goal onto the graph's concepts, finds the talks that teach them, and plans the main pick.
actions: Type the goal into Ask the graph, Send, live agent call (wait shortened in the edit).

caption: Picks light up on the map. 'Why this answer?' shows every step
voiceover: The picks light up on the map, with cards that say why each one fits. And the agent can only answer through graph tools. 'Why this answer?' lists every step it took, and the graph queries are one click away.
actions: Show highlighted talks and cards, open Why this answer? and See the graph queries.

caption: One talk: "Own your Copilot", an advanced Thursday workshop
voiceover: Now, a single talk: Own your Copilot, an advanced workshop on Thursday. 'About this talk' is an AI summary of the abstract, the concepts it assumes and teaches, and a few outside readings that Bright Data found and OpenAI vetted.
actions: Open the talk page for BLD1428W, open About this talk.

caption: Newcomer: 4 steps, one multi-hop DEPENDS_ON query
voiceover: For a newcomer, the graph unfolds four steps. The talk assumes you know how to use GitHub Copilot, and Copilot customization in turn depends on Copilot basics, Git, and the command line. That's one multi-hop query over the graph's depends-on links. The day plan says where to learn each step: a Wednesday talk, or a short explainer.
actions: Show the path graph and the day plan.

caption: Profile: "Some experience" skips the basics
voiceover: Tell it about yourself. With some experience, the basics are skipped. Same talk, and now just one step.
actions: Set up profile, choose Some experience, Save, re-plan.

caption: Click any step: the exact quote behind each link
voiceover: Click any step to see the evidence. Every link carries the exact words from a talk's title or abstract, checked word for word, or it's thrown out. Here, a Wednesday workshop teaches Copilot customization.
actions: Click the remaining concept node, show its quote and where to learn it.

caption: "I attended this": the clock moves, the plan re-runs
voiceover: It's Wednesday afternoon, and I went to that workshop. Everything it teaches now counts as learned, the clock moves to the end of the talk, and the plan runs again. You're ready. That memory lives in the graph, and 'Forget me' deletes it.
actions: Open the teaching talk from the day plan, click I attended this, show You're ready.

caption: FalkorDB at the core · Bright Data for hard-to-reach data · OpenAI agent
voiceover: How it's built. FalkorDB is the core: multi-hop prerequisite paths, the prepares-you-for flow, and each attendee's memory, all in the graph. The agent can write its own read-only Cypher, but only against a copy of the graph with no attendee data. Bright Data brings in the hard-to-reach data: the JavaScript-rendered catalog, nearby conferences, explainers and readings. OpenAI extracted the concepts with word-for-word evidence, and runs the agent.
actions: Back to the conference map; gentle hovers.

caption: 400 of 401 links passed the word-for-word check
voiceover: Honestly measured: 400 of 401 proposed links passed the word-for-word check, and an AI review of 20 random links found 15 correct, 5 partly right, and none wrong. Throughline: find your conference, tell it your goal, and walk in ready.
